title: Building Multi agent Systems with Finite State Machines
talk_summary: The talk argues that multi-agent systems should combine actor-style message passing with finite-state/statechart workflows so LLM autonomy is bounded by explicit states, guards, and transitions. It demos patterns from tool use and human approval to critic feedback, collaboration, LLM-selected transitions, and LLM-generated statecharts, emphasizing replayability and testability.

takeaways.evidence_quote: we apply a guard which enforces valid transitions

takeaways.what_they_do: Persist every transition event so current state can be reconstructed by replay; replay to a point and branch to recover.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if you lose your current state you can actually recalculate it by playing your replaying your log of events

takeaways.what_they_do: Generate tests from the FSM definition so every valid transition/guard is exercised.
takeaways.evidence_quote: modelbased testing where you can be programmatically certain that your tests are exercising every valid transition

takeaways.what_they_do: For multi-step workflows, define compensating actions to undo prior steps when a later step fails.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if a step in the process fails you can apply compensating transactions to undo the previous steps

takeaways.technique: Human approval state for risky tools
takeaways.what_they_do: Insert an approval state before risky tool calls and wait for an authenticated/authorized message to continue.
takeaways.evidence_quote: add an intermediate intermediate approval step and wait for an authenticated and authorized message

takeaways.what_they_do: Let an LLM planner choose among event emitters, but enforce transition guards so it can only move to valid next states.
